title: The split torus over a scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $r\in\mathbf N$. Put $A=\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$. Let $A[\mathbf Z^r]$ be the commutative group algebra consisting of finite sums $\sum_m a_me_m$, with $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$. Give it the Hopf structure $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, $e_m\mapsto1$, and $e_m\mapsto e_{-m}$. Define the split torus $T_{S,r}=(\mathbf G_{m,S})^r$ as the base change $S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A[\mathbf Z^r])$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-pc-fibre-product] along the canonical map $S\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, with the group law induced by this Hopf structure. The rank-zero case is the trivial group over $S$. No field, affineness, or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed on $S$.
